how-we-make-money.title: How we make money
how-we-make-money.summary: We earn a commission from prop firms when you buy through us, and we give most of it back.

sections.heading: Commission
body: When you buy a challenge using our link or code, the prop firm pays us a commission, usually a percentage of the fee. Rates differ by firm. We only earn when the firm confirms the purchase.
We return most of that commission to you as Coins. The share depends on your level and on any active season, and it is published in How rewards work.

sections.heading: Other income
body: Pro membership, which you can pay for with Coins or cash. Sponsored placements, which are always labelled Sponsored and never change how firms are ordered or scored. Firm-sponsored contests. Affiliate links for trading tools, which are disclosed where they appear.

sections.heading: What we never do
body: We don't sell your personal data. We don't let commission rates or sponsorship affect rankings or scores. We don't reward you for buying again after a failed challenge.

how-rewards-work.title: How rewards work
how-rewards-work.summary: Coins come only from confirmed purchases and funded campaigns. XP comes from using the site.

sections.heading: Coins
body: When the firm confirms your purchase, we credit a share of our commission to you as Coins. They are pending until the commission is confirmed and 14 days have passed since the purchase, then they become available.
If a purchase is refunded or charged back, the Coins from it are reversed.

Coins have no cash value, cannot be withdrawn, sold or transferred, and are redeemed for rewards such as challenge accounts. Coins expire after 12 months with no sign-in, earning or redemption; we warn you 30 and 7 days before.

sections.heading: How many Coins
body: Coins = commission × your give-back share. The default shares by level are Bronze 60%, Silver 64%, Gold 68%, Platinum 72% and Black 75%. During the Founding Season everyone gets 90%. The total paid out on any purchase, including boosters and referral bonuses, never exceeds 95% of the commission.

sections.heading: XP and levels
body: XP comes from check-ins, missions, lessons, the journal and tools. XP never turns into Coins. Levels need both XP and verified purchases, and they never go down.

how-we-rank-firms.title: How we order and score firms
how-we-rank-firms.summary: Rankings use prices, rules and verified data only. Commission and sponsorship are never inputs.

sections.heading: Sorting
body: You choose the order: net price, list price, newest or name. Net price is list price minus the active discount minus the value of Coins you would get back.

sections.heading: Scores and status
body: Any score we publish will be explained on this page, with its inputs, before it goes live. Firms may carry a Watch or Delisted status when we see problems such as delayed payouts or changed rules; the reason is shown on the firm's page.

sections.heading: Sponsored placements
body: Firms can pay for labelled placements. A sponsored slot always says Sponsored and never moves a firm up a sorted list.

affiliate-disclosure.title: Affiliate disclosure
affiliate-disclosure.summary: We are paid when you buy through our links and codes.

sections.heading: Our relationship with firms
body: {brand} is an affiliate of the prop firms listed. When you buy through our link or use our code, the firm pays us a commission. This does not change the price you pay.
We share most of that commission with you as Coins, but only for firms that have given us written permission to do so. Other firms are listed and compared, and show that rewards are not available.

risk-disclosure.title: Risk disclosure
risk-disclosure.summary: Prop firm challenges are simulated evaluations. Most traders don't pass.

sections.heading: Challenges are not investments
body: A challenge fee pays for a simulated trading evaluation. It is not a deposit or an investment, and it is not refundable unless the firm says so. Most traders do not pass, and many who pass never receive a payout.
Prop firms are often lightly regulated and some have closed or refused payouts. Read each firm's terms before you buy.

sections.heading: No advice
body: {brand} does not give investment, trading or financial advice. Our tools help you follow rules and review your own trading; they do not tell you what to trade.

sections.heading: Where offers are unavailable
body: Some offers are not shown in some countries because of local rules. For example, forex and CFD prop offers are not shown to residents of India.

sections.heading: Who can use the site
body: You must be 18 or older and may hold one account. Accounts found to be duplicates may be closed and their rewards removed.

sections.heading: Your conduct
body: Don't submit false claims, reuse receipts, automate the site, or try to get around geographic restrictions. We may freeze rewards while we review suspicious activity.

sections.heading: Changes and contact
body: We may update these terms and will tell you about material changes. Questions: {email}.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.summary: What we collect, why, and for how long.

sections.heading: What we collect
body: Your email, country, time zone and the 18+ confirmation; purchase claims and receipts you upload; your activity on the site; and a hashed form of your IP address for fraud prevention. Waitlist members: email, a hashed IP and the referral link used.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
body: Receipts and payout proofs: 24 months unless tied to an open dispute. Hashed IPs rotate monthly. When you delete your account, personal data is removed; ledger and claim records are kept without personal details for accounting.

sections.heading: Your rights
body: You can export your data or delete your account from Profile, or email {email}. Your trading journal is private: our staff cannot read it unless you grant time-limited access.

rewards-terms.title: Rewards terms
rewards-terms.summary: The rules for Coins, XP and redemptions.

sections.heading: Coins
body: Coins are a loyalty reward with no cash value. They cannot be exchanged for money, crypto or gift cards, transferred, or sold. Earning rates are set in How rewards work and may change for future purchases; Coins already credited keep their value.

sections.heading: Redemptions
body: When a reward is in stock, its code is shown at once. When it is not, the redemption is queued with a 48-hour target and you are told at every step.

sections.heading: Chance-based features
body: Any spin or draw is free to enter, never tied to purchases, publishes its odds, and is not offered where local law does not allow it.

lot-size.title: Prop lot size calculator
lot-size.metaDescription: Calculate lots for a set risk and stop loss, with correct pip sizes for JPY pairs, gold, silver and indices. Warns when a loss would exceed your daily room.
lot-size.short: Lots for a set risk and stop, with pip value and money at risk.
lot-size.intro: Enter your balance, how much you want to risk and your stop. The size rounds down to your broker's lot step, so the trade never risks more than you set.

risk.label: Risk per trade
risk.hint: A percentage of the balance, or an amount in the account currency.

dailyRoom.label: Daily room left (optional)
dailyRoom.hint: From the daily room calculator. Used to warn you before a trade that could breach the daily limit.

stop.label: Stop loss distance
stop.hint: In pips, or as a price difference such as 0.0020.

price.label: {symbol} price
price.hint: Needed because {account} is the base currency of this pair.

lotStep.label: Lot step
lotStep.hint: The smallest size change your platform allows.

contract.label: Contract size (optional)
contract.hint: Units per 1.00 lot. Default for {symbol}: {size}. Check your platform's contract specification.

notes.belowMinimum: Your risk is smaller than the smallest position. One lot step risks {amount} at this stop.
notes.exceedsDailyRoom: This loss is larger than your remaining daily room. Hitting the stop would breach the daily limit.

explain: Risk amount is the balance times the risk percentage, or the fixed amount you enter.

Pip value per lot is the pip size times the contract size, converted into your account currency. A pip is 0.0001 on most pairs, 0.01 on JPY pairs, 0.10 on gold and 0.01 on silver. Indices use one point.
Lots equal the risk amount divided by the stop in pips times the pip value per lot, rounded down to your lot step. Money at risk is then recalculated from the rounded size.
Contract sizes for metals and indices differ between brokers. Enter the figure from your platform when it differs from the default.

pip-value.title: Pip value and margin calculator
pip-value.metaDescription: Calculate pip value, position value and required margin for forex pairs, gold, silver and indices in your account currency.
pip-value.short: Pip value, position value and the margin a trade needs.
pip-value.intro: Enter the instrument, size and current price. Margin depends on your account leverage, which your firm sets.

price.label: {symbol} price
price.hint: The current price on your platform.

contract.label: Contract size (optional)
contract.hint: Units per 1.00 lot. Default for {symbol}: {size}. Check your platform's contract specification.

explain: Pip value equals the pip size times the contract size times the lots, converted into your account currency.
Position value equals the lots times the contract size times the price, converted into your account currency. Margin required is the position value divided by the leverage.
Firms often set different leverage for forex, metals and indices. Check your program's rules.

daily-room.title: Daily room calculator
daily-room.metaDescription: See how much you can lose today before your prop firm's daily loss or max loss limit, for static, trailing and end-of-day trailing drawdown.
daily-room.short: How much you can lose today before the daily or max loss limit.
daily-room.intro: Enter your program's limits and today's figures. The calculator shows the room left before each limit and which one is closer.

dailyBasis.label: Daily limit is a percentage of

lock.label: Trailing stops at the starting size

dayStart.label: Balance or equity at today's reset
dayStart.hint: Use the figure your firm measures from at its daily reset time.

peak.label: Highest point reached
peak.hint: Highest equity for intraday trailing, or highest end-of-day balance for end-of-day trailing.

stopPips.label: Stop loss in pips (optional)
stopPips.hint: Add a stop to see the largest position that fits inside the room.

price.label: {symbol} price
price.hint: Needed because {account} is the base currency of this pair.

notes.breached: Equity is at or below a limit. Check your firm's dashboard: the account may already be breached.
notes.close: You are within 20% of the daily limit.
notes.bindingDaily: The daily limit is the closer limit today.
notes.bindingMax: The max loss limit is closer than the daily limit.

explain: Equity equals the balance plus open profit or loss plus open commission and swap.
The daily limit level is today's reset figure minus the daily limit. The limit is a percentage of either the starting size or today's figure, depending on your firm.

A static max loss stays at the starting size minus the max loss. An intraday trailing level rises with the highest equity reached. An end-of-day trailing level rises only with the highest closing balance. Some firms stop the trailing level once it reaches the starting size.
Firms word these rules differently. Check your program's rules page: this calculator cannot know your firm's exact method.

payout.title: Payout calculator
payout.metaDescription: Estimate a prop firm payout after profit split, buffer, minimum payout and fees, with an expected arrival date.
payout.short: What you receive after split, buffer and fees, and when.
payout.intro: Enter your profit and your program's payout terms. The result shows your share, what arrives after fees, and an estimated date.

buffer.label: Buffer kept in the account (optional)
buffer.hint: Some firms require part of the profit to stay in the account.

notes.belowMinimum: Your share is below the minimum payout. You need {amount} more profit to request it.

explain: Eligible profit equals the profit minus the buffer. Your share is the eligible profit times your split. You receive your share minus the payout fee.
The estimated date adds the processing time in business days, Monday to Friday, to the request date. Bank holidays and firm reviews can add time.
Payouts depend on each firm's rules and reviews. A calculated amount is not a promise that a firm will pay.

risk-reward.title: Risk/reward calculator
risk-reward.metaDescription: Calculate reward per unit of risk and the breakeven win rate for a given gain and loss.
risk-reward.short: Reward per unit of risk and the win rate needed to break even.
risk-reward.intro: Enter a potential loss and gain in the same currency, after fees. The result shows the win rate needed to break even at those amounts.
explain: Reward per unit of risk divides gain by loss. The breakeven win rate divides loss by the sum of gain and loss.
Both calculations assume the amounts stay the same across trades.

drawdown-recovery.title: Drawdown recovery calculator
drawdown-recovery.metaDescription: Calculate the percentage gain needed to recover from a drawdown, and the amount to regain.
drawdown-recovery.short: The gain you need to get back to where you started.
drawdown-recovery.intro: A loss takes a larger percentage gain to recover, because the gain is made on a smaller balance.
explain: The gain needed equals the loss divided by 100 minus the loss, times 100. A 10% loss needs an 11.1% gain. A 50% loss needs 100%.
In a prop challenge, the max loss limit usually ends the account long before a deep drawdown could be recovered.

sessions.marketClosed: Forex market closed for the weekend
sessions.timelineCaption: Today's sessions on a 24-hour timeline in your timezone, with overlaps and the current time.
explain: Each session runs from 08:00 to 17:00 local time in London and New York, 09:00 to 18:00 in Tokyo and 07:00 to 16:00 in Sydney. These are the common conventions; liquidity builds and fades gradually rather than at exact times.

The daily rollover, when swap is charged, and the weekly close and open are at 17:00 New York time. Many firms do not allow holding positions over the weekend: check your program's rules before the Friday close.
Bank holidays are not shown yet.

consistency.title: Consistency rule calculator
consistency.metaDescription: Check a prop firm consistency rule: your largest day's share of profit, the profit still needed before a payout, and the most you can make today.
consistency.short: Your best day's share of profit and how much more you need before a payout.
consistency.intro: Many funded programs cap how much of your total profit can come from one day. Enter your profit so far and your best day to see where you stand.

bestDay.label: Largest single-day profit
bestDay.hint: Your best day so far, in the same currency.

limit.label: Largest day allowed (% of total profit)
limit.hint: From your program's rules, for example 30.

notes.passes: Your best day is within the rule.
notes.fails: Your best day is above the limit. Keep trading to the rule until total profit reaches the figure above.

explain: Best day's share equals your largest single-day profit divided by total profit.

For the rule to pass, total profit must be at least the best day divided by the limit. Today breaks the rule only if it becomes your largest day and its share goes over the limit; that happens above the limit times profit so far, divided by one minus the limit.
Firms apply consistency rules differently: some count only payout periods, some include today's open profit. Check your program's rules page.

challenge-cost.title: Challenge cost calculator
challenge-cost.metaDescription: Work out the cost per prop firm challenge attempt after a discount, the total for several attempts, and the payout needed to break even.
challenge-cost.short: Cost per attempt, total for several attempts and the break-even payout.
challenge-cost.intro: See what a challenge really costs if it takes more than one attempt. Most traders do not pass, so plan for the number of attempts you can afford.

rows.breakEvenProfit: Funded profit needed to break even

notes.odds: Challenges are simulated evaluations and most traders do not pass. Only spend what you can afford to lose.

explain: Cost per attempt equals the fee minus the discount. The total multiplies it by the attempts.
If the firm refunds the fee with the first payout, the passing attempt's fee comes back, so only the other attempts need to be covered. Funded profit needed divides that payout by your split.
Coins earned on a purchase are rewards with no cash value and are not counted here.
